title: VaiVia route document
description: The product: one route, as every reader consumes it. PostGIS holds the value; this is what is delivered. See docs/route-document.md for the reasoning behind each block. Readers outlive producers, so this is versioned and additive: a new field is a minor version, a removed or re-meaning field is a major one.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Readers must tolerate an unknown minor.

id.description: Stable across rebuilds. A comment or photo keys to this, so a route that regenerates to the same ground must keep its id, and a route that genuinely changes gets a new one rather than mutating. See docs/social-layer.md.

kind.description: osm_route is a route somebody mapped; generated is one this pipeline drew. Same document either way.

identity.description: How a walker recognises this route. ref and the painted waymark matter more than the name here: most CAI sentieri have a number and no name.

network.description: OSM scope: lwn/rwn/nwn/iwn walking, lcn/rcn/ncn cycling

waymark.description: osmc:symbol, the paint on the rock

geometry.description: The map. WGS84 (EPSG:4326). A MultiLineString is not an error: it is a route this network holds in pieces, and continuity says so.

bbox.description: [minx, miny, maxx, maxy], so a reader can index and cull without parsing the geometry

measures.description: duration is deliberately absent: DIN 33466 rates the classic Grigna ascent at 10 h against a guidebook 6-8, so the figure this codebase can compute is one a user would not trust. An absent field invites the calibration; a wrong one ships.

ascent_m.description: null when any edge lacks a profile. Absent is not zero: a partial sum would read as a flat route.

profile.description: The altitude profile, as two parallel arrays of equal length. Null rather than partial when any sample is missing.

surface.description: A distribution kept whole, plus a dominant value. '62% unpaved' is a fact about a route; 'unpaved' alone is a claim. Untagged length is reported as 'unknown' rather than renormalised away.

difficulty.description: Two grades, both true: sac_scale is the CHARACTER (hardest grade covering >=5% of the length - a label), sac_max the EXIGENT grade (hardest graded metre, any length - what you must be able to handle; owner rule 2026-08-20). graded_share says how much of the route carries any grade, so sparse grading reads as a mapping fact rather than a failed join. The rule ships with the numbers.

sac_scale.description: The hardest grade covering at least 5% of the length, never the max: 30 m of scramble must not label a 20 km valley walk alpine.

sac_max.description: The hardest graded metre walked, however short.

graded_share.description: Share of the length carrying any recognised sac_scale.

start.description: Where a walk on this route can begin. names is often empty because car parks are rarely named in OSM: a known gap, not a bug.

places.description: What the route passes, ordered along it. Bounded at 100 m, which is where qa.distance_band puts 'near'; offset_m travels so a reader wanting 30 m filters on it. distance_along_m is null on a route held in more than one piece, because there is no single measure along it.

ele_m.description: The OSM ele tag, never the DEM: a 30 m cell reads a summit ~23 m low by design.

quality.description: Carried, never filtered on. A route this network holds in three pieces is still a real route, and the reader deciding whether to show it needs to know which one it is.

matched_fraction.description: osm_route only: the share of the relation's ways this network holds. Null for a generated route - absent is not zero.

provenance.description: Attribution travels INSIDE the document. The document is the Produced Work under ODbL, so a consumer that renders the geometry elsewhere cannot strip the obligation by accident.
